description:
## Current scope
The three DuckDB measurements have passed. The remaining decision is whether to accept the resulting all-platform release-gate expansion; successful DuckDB runs do not authorize that expansion.

## Historical finding (retained for provenance)
## Problem
`read_primitives` lists 0.01 and 0.1 as standard while its siblings `write_primitives` and `transaction_primitives` list 1.0 on the same TPC-H data. `clickbench` lists only 1.0. The site tables present `read_primitives` 1.0 and `clickbench` 0.01 and 0.1 as ordinary use cases, so following the docs prints the note that results are not comparable with published results. The site now marks those rows as outside the standard set (benchbox-site#142), but the lists were not widened: both DuckDB attempts on 2026-11-11 were stopped by the heavy-work watchdog under host memory pressure, so no passing run exists.

## Change
Run `read_primitives` at SF 1 and `clickbench` at SF 0.01 and 0.1 on DuckDB through `make heavy-run`. If they pass, add the values to `scale_options` in `benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.yaml` and remove the three site notes.

## Guardrails
- A new standard value joins the interactive options and the UAT matrix filter (`tests/uat/matrix.py` `filter_scales_by_registry`); check the UAT time budget.
- Site edits go through a benchbox-site pull request.

## Decision gates
DuckDB measurements already passed: read_primitives SF 1 = 612/612 in 31 s; ClickBench SF 0.01/0.1 = 172/172 in 3/7 s on 3f8cf88f4a. Owner must choose widening versus retaining notes after enumerating every newly admitted UAT platform cell and budget impact. Do not automatically widen from DuckDB success.

## Verification rubric
Pass: exact matrix delta, affected eligibility/pair floors and standard/non-standard UI/MCP behavior are recorded. If widened, affected cells execute within their budgets, registry validation tests pass and site next agrees. If retained, document the choice and keep accurate notes.

## Additional guardrails
Do not silently prune failing added cells or lower floors to conceal them. Standard-list changes do not alter global accepted range. No new cloud cells run without spend approval.
